title: Complete blood count
what: This test shows how many red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets you have, and your hemoglobin level. It is the most common blood test.
why: For checkups, before surgery, and when you have a fever, weakness, or a possible anemia or inflammation.
duration: the blood draw takes 3 to 5 minutes; results usually come the next day
tell_doctor: If you were recently ill or had a fever
If you are having your period right now

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Morning is best, either fasting or a few hours after a light meal. Ask the lab.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: No alcohol and no hard workouts.

steps: Blood is taken from a vein or a fingertip
A band, antiseptic, and a quick prick
Blood fills a tube, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
after: Press the cotton pad for a few minutes
Your doctor will explain the results. Numbers alone are not a diagnosis

faq.a: It is how fast red blood cells settle in a tube. It goes up with inflammation, but can also be high without illness. Your doctor will judge it.
It is better, but not strictly needed. After a fatty meal, the result may be less accurate.

reminders.text: Blood count test tomorrow. Try not to eat in the morning. Water is fine.
